text.p: Mexican stocks extended their early gains on an announcement of government loan prepayments to reach the 3,700-point barrier for the first time ever in mid-afternoon trade on Wednesday.
The leading IPC share index was up 70.78 points, or 1.95 percent, at 3,702.14.

Traders said that share prices had rallied on an announcement by Finance Minister Guillermo Ortiz that Mexico would pay the U.S. Treasury remaining $3.5 billion outstanding on an emergency loan granted in February 1995, and an additional $1.5 billion to the International Monetary Fund.

"Basically what (the announcment) did was ease pressure and help to remove any remaining uncertainty among investors as to the prospects for economic growth this year," a broker said. The ebullient mood abroad in the market was reflected in trading volume .TV.MX of 138.5 million shares, which was heavy even after discounting hefty cross trades.
